record.title: ROBOTIS DYNAMIXEL XL330-M288-T - 18 g smart servo, 288.4:1, TTL multidrop bus, Protocol 2.0
record.origin_why: Every electrical, register, connector and dimensional figure in this folder was read off ROBOTIS's own pages and files, fetched 2026-09-02 and hashed in PROVENANCE.json: the e-Manual product page (E1), its docs.robotis.com successor (E2), the 'XL,XC-330.pdf' drawing (D1), the moment-of-inertia sheet (D2) and the vendor STEP body (S1). No published standard defines this actuator, so `standard` is wrong; nobody here has put an instrument on one, so `measured` is wrong. The GEOMETRY has a different origin and says so: cad/part.py was measured off Pollen's published mesh (see its docstring) and is graded against it in evidence/refcheck; the vendor's own STEP now sits in iterations/v0.0.1/geometry/ with its provenance.
record.lifecycle_why: No fetched vendor page states a lifecycle. The e-Manual banner says the manual site itself is being retired in favour of docs.robotis.com, which is about the documentation, not the part. robotis.us listed it InStock at $27.49 on 2026-09-02 (sourcing.json), which is availability, not lifecycle.
record.why: IDENTITY AND FIGURES ARE SOURCED; the folder still cannot say PASS for two measured reasons. (1) The design runs this part outside its published band: electrical.chip.json supplies[0] is 3.7-6.0 V verbatim, the Microduck's pack is 6.6-8.2 V through the servos' own Present Input Voltage(144), and Pollen's robotd clears the Input Voltage Error shutdown bit (52 vs vendor default 53). RESEARCHED AND ANSWERED 2026-09-02 (lane C), record.voltage_band_verdict: Pollen's own runtime says in a comment that the voltage the servos report IS the pack ('the pack seen through the bus', research/raw/duck-control_src_model.rs:102-112), so the servos DO see 6.6-8.2 V, and Shutdown(63) = 52 switches off the very fault that arrangement would otherwise trip continuously. The design runs this part outside its published band with its own over-voltage protection disabled — a FAIL against the vendor's rating, with the stall-current and stall-heating extrapolation quantified in that record. It stays CANNOT DETERMINE and not FAIL here only because that is Pollen's word in a source comment and not a meter on a production robot's servo VDD pin, which is what would close it. (2) cad/interfaces.json still declares no interfaces (the horn / idler / side-mount frames measured in cad/part.py are not yet written as interfaces), so bin/triad check has nothing to measure there. electrical.chip.json lists nine further recorded unknowns.

voltage_band_verdict.$about: Answering 'whether production Microducks run stock XL330s over their rating'. Researched 2026-09-02 (lane C). The answer is in Pollen's own source, in a comment.
voltage_band_verdict.verdict: FAIL against the vendor's rating. The servos are powered from the raw 2S pack — 6.6 V to 8.2 V — which is 0.6 V to 2.2 V above the XL330's published 6.0 V maximum at EVERY state of charge, and the servo's own over-voltage shutdown is deliberately switched off in firmware so that it cannot object.
voltage_band_verdict.the_rating: ROBOTIS e-Manual, XL330-M288-T, §Specifications, verbatim: 'Input Voltage | 3.7 ~ 6.0 [V] (Recommended : 5.0 [V])'. There is no absolute-maximum table; the only other ceiling the vendor states is §Control Table 'Max Voltage Limit(32) ... Range 31 ~ 70 ... Unit 0.1 [V]' — the firmware CANNOT BE TOLD to accept more than 7.0 V.
voltage_band_verdict.the_proof_that_the_pack_reaches_the_serv: research/raw/duck-control_src_model.rs:102-112, Pollen's own comment, verbatim: 'There is no fuel gauge and no ADC. The only measurement available is what the servos report as their own supply (`crate::bus::DynamixelIo::bus_voltage`), which is THE PACK SEEN THROUGH THE BUS — so it sags under load and recovers when the robot stands still.' Followed by `pub const BATTERY_FULL_V: f64 = 8.2;` ('Off a full charge, under load. NP-F550, 2S Li-ion.') and `pub const BATTERY_EMPTY_V: f64 = 6.6;`. If a regulator sat between the pack and the servos, Present Input Voltage(144) would read a constant and would be useless as the fuel gauge Pollen uses it as.
voltage_band_verdict.the_corroboration: research/raw/duck-control_src_model.rs:93, in SERVO_EEPROM: ('shutdown', 52). The vendor initial value of Shutdown(63) is 53 = 0b00110101. 52 = 0b00110100 clears exactly one bit, Bit 0, 'Input Voltage Error ... Detects that input voltage exceeds the configured operating voltage'. Clearing it makes sense ONLY if the servo's supply can leave the [Min Voltage Limit, Max Voltage Limit] window — and with a 5 V regulated rail it never could, because 5.0 V sits comfortably inside the default 3.5-7.0 V window. Pollen switched off the fault that its own supply arrangement would otherwise trip continuously.

how_far_over.at_pack_full_8_2V: 1.367x the 6.0 V maximum, 1.640x the 5.0 V recommended point
how_far_over.the_firmware_ceiling: 8.2 V exceeds even Max Voltage Limit(32)'s largest settable value, 7.0 V, by 1.2 V

reliability_consequence.$basis: DERIVED by linear extrapolation of the vendor's own three stall rows, stated as an extrapolation because the vendor publishes nothing above 6.0 V. §Specifications 'Stall Torque': '0.42 [N.m] (at 3.7 [V], 1.11 [A])', '0.52 [N.m] (at 5.0 [V], 1.47 [A])', '0.60 [N.m] (at 6.0 [V], 1.74 [A])'. A least-squares fit of I = V/R through the origin over those three points gives R = 3.4104 ohm and reproduces them to within 2.3 %, 0.3 % and 1.1 % — so the motor+driver looks resistive over the published band.
reliability_consequence.stall_heating: Stall power in the winding goes as V^2/R. At 8.2 V that is 19.72 W per servo against 7.35 W at the recommended 5.0 V — 2.68x the heat, into a 20.0 x 34.0 x 26.0 mm plastic-cased 18 g actuator whose vendor operating range ends at +70 degC. The gear train, rated for the 0.60 N.m the vendor states at 6.0 V, would see roughly 0.83 N.m at stall at 8.2 V on the same fit.
reliability_consequence.fleet_current: 15 servos at 8.2 V stall extrapolates to 36.07 A through one bus and one pack. The vendor's own worst published figure, 15 x 1.74 A at 6.0 V, is 26.1 A. Nothing Pollen publishes states what the pack or the HAT's power path can deliver.
reliability_consequence.what_is_not_claimed: No failure has been observed here and none is predicted with a rate. Robots ship and walk. The measured statement is narrower and harder: THE DESIGN OPERATES A COMPONENT OUTSIDE ITS PUBLISHED BAND WITH THE COMPONENT'S OWN PROTECTION FOR THAT CASE DISABLED, so the servo's rated life and the vendor's warranty do not cover the way it is used, and the margin against thermal or gear failure is unknown rather than small.

voltage_band_verdict.what_would_settle_the_remaining_doubt: A meter on servo VDD on a production robot, at full charge, with the robot standing. If it reads the pack, this verdict is confirmed by measurement rather than by Pollen's comment; if it reads ~5 V, then a regulator exists that no source mentions and the fuel gauge works by some other route. Second: ROBOTIS confirming (or denying) an OEM XL330 variant binned for a higher supply — none is published.
voltage_band_verdict.what_a_manufacturer_should_do_with_this: Either accept the derating and say so in the product's own documentation (with a thermal test at 8.2 V behind it), or put a 5.0-6.0 V regulator in the servo path and find another source for the state-of-charge reading. The second costs a buck converter rated for the fleet current above; the first costs a test.
